summary: The sketch solver now splits a sketch into independent groups (geometry joined by shared points and relations) and solves each group in its own native system. Geometry without relations keeps its values without loading the native solver, and every unfixed coordinate or radius in it counts as one degree of freedom, as before. Relations on fully fixed geometry are solved with the smallest group that has unknowns, because PlaneGCS diagnoses nothing in a system without unknowns; they are still reported as redundant or conflicting as before. Native work runs one solve at a time. Freedom is summed and conflicting, redundant and partially redundant relations are combined across groups, with the same rejection order as before. Before any native call, one group whose unfixed parameters times scalar equations exceeds 500,000 (coincident, midpoint and symmetric relations count two equations) is rejected with the new too-large reason and a message to split it, instead of risking an out-of-memory abort. After a native abort, the solver runtime discards the module before its next solve; the worker resets its module for that. On the benchmark, independent fully constrained rectangles now solve up to at least 400 in one sketch, where 100 previously aborted with out of memory.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Saved documents keep their schema and contents. Diagnostics for the existing workloads and tests are identical. Behavior change: one connected group of relations above the limit (for example 89 or more chained, fully constrained rectangles) is now refused as too large when it is solved, where some such groups up to about 100 rectangles solved before. The solver result protocol gains the too-large rejection reason, shown as sketch-too-large in sketch edit feedback.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage or journal schema change. The internal sketch solver reply adds the too-large reason. Post engine API remains 1; saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, WebMCP tool, cancellation or input-version behavior change.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: New runtime tests show that a sketch with a fixed line, a redundant group, a conflicting group and free circles reports the same freedom and relation identities as each group alone; that a relation on expression-fixed geometry is still rejected as redundant or conflicting; that 399 chained coincidences, whose native diagnosis aborted, are refused as too large; that geometry without relations solves without loading the native module; that 89 chained rectangles are refused as too large before native code while 88 solve; that 150 independent rectangles, which aborted as one system, now solve; and that an aborted module is discarded before the next solve, or reported clearly when it cannot be, including for two overlapping solves. A differential probe against the previous single-system runtime returned identical results for fixed, conflicting, redundant, coincidence-chain and rectangle workloads. All existing CAD and sketch solver suites pass unchanged, together with native tsc -b and npm run lint with zero findings. The benchmark probes independent and connected capacity and records parameters and constraints.

changes: Sketches with many separate groups of relations no longer run the sketch solver out of memory.
One very large connected group of relations now shows a clear message asking you to split it, instead of failing.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: If a sketch reports that a connected group of relations is too large, split it into separate groups or remove relations.
